predecessors.name: Kingdom of Sweden
predecessors.text: Finland within its present borders as the nearest named region to the ceded Swedish Finland, with Aland and the lands east of the Tornio and Muonio rivers

predecessors.name: Russian Empire
predecessors.text: Old Finland: the Viipuri (Vyborg) Province of the Karelian Isthmus and the Ladoga shore, annexed by Russia in 1721 and 1743

successors.name: Republic of Finland
successors.text: Finland after the Declaration of Independence of 6 December 1917

ledger.x: 1809, 29 March: the four estates assembled at the Diet of Porvoo pledge allegiance to Alexander I as Grand Duke of Finland; Russia had invaded Finland in February 1808.

1809, 17 September: by the Treaty of Fredrikshamn Sweden gives Russia "its Finnish territories, the Aland islands, and parts of Lappland and Vasterbotten east of the Tornio and Muonio rivers"; the territory becomes the autonomous Grand Duchy.
1812: the capital moves from Turku to Helsinki.
1812: Alexander I transfers the Vyborg Governorate (Old Finland, annexed by Russia in 1721 and 1743) "from Russia proper to the grand duchy", announced on 23 December 1811 O.S.
1917, 6 December: "the Finnish Parliament approved the Declaration of Independence" after the collapse of the Russian monarchy; the Grand Duchy becomes the Republic of Finland.

wars.name: Finnish War
wars.outcome: Russian victory: Sweden cedes Finland, Aland and the lands east of the Tornio and Muonio rivers by the Treaty of Fredrikshamn (17 September 1809).

certainty.note: The Tornio and Muonio rivers and the Treaty of Fredrikshamn line in the north-west, and the 1721 and 1743 lines of Old Finland in the east.
